Hi Alex — quick technical note on function-calling / schema compliance and retries so you have something to share with your infra folks: 

1) How Redwood surfaces function-call errors
- Our runtime supports both "tool" (function) responses and structured output. When a model returns partial/invalid JSON we surface a parsing error in the response envelope: {status: "invalid_schema", details: "parse_error at offset 248"}. We will not automatically mutate your downstream state.

2) Recommended retry/backoff policy
- Idempotency: include an idempotency token (e.g., ticket_id + run_id) with each ingest; use Upsert semantics on your side to prevent duplicate processing.
- Retry window: short exponential backoff (100ms -> 500ms -> 2s) up to 3 attempts for transient errors (parse/timeout). If parsing consistently fails we return the original response and flag for human review.

3) Prompt / validator strategy we’ll apply in the eval
- Use a schema-first prompt wrapper: "Return ONLY valid JSON matching schema X. If you are unsure, return {\"error\":\"UNCERTAIN\"}."
- Add a validator step in the pipeline: fast synthetic type checks + a strict JSON Schema validator; failures are routed to the fallback policy (retry/alternative model).

4) Cost notes for the 5k eval (ballpark)
- Redwood-2-small: ~ $120 (compute + tokens)
- RWX-13B-quant: ~ $270
- Includes 3 prompt variations x 5k samples and schema validation pass. We can reduce permutations to lower cost.

I started a quick initial run on a 500-sample subset using the prompt_set_v2; attaching eval_summary_20271102.csv with sample metrics (schema pass rate, entity F1, avg latency). Full run pending your S3 link.

Happy to join the Thursday follow-up. If you want, Marissa can schedule the 30-min slot.
